ce_bugs.text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1873 — Persisting only destinationCalendar[0] discards secondary collective hosts, so later confirmation or payment flows never create their calendar events.
packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 — Every collective host credential targets the first host's Lark calendar, causing secondary-host creates to fail or hit the wrong calendar.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — Every collective host credential targets the first host's Office 365 calendar, causing secondary-host creates to fail or hit the wrong calendar.
packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156 — Secondary CalDAV credentials filter against the first host's calendar and report success when the empty match set creates no event.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — Recurring collective cancellation deletes through only the organizer's credentials and first reference, leaving secondary-host events orphaned while repeating organizer deletes.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:591 — A multi-calendar update exception is silently converted into batch failures without logging, allowing reschedule state to advance while external calendars diverge.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:168 — Google creation can insert into primary but patch with an undefined calendarId and still resolve success, silently losing the Meet-description update.

mrv_findings.text: P1 confidence 100 — packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")` — Events without a destination calendar dereference `undefined`, so Google Meet fallback crashes before integrations can be created.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254 — `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — The falsey branch searches for that same falsey ID and passes `undefined` as Google's required `calendarId`, making updates fail whenever no explicit external ID is supplied.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/core/EventManager.ts:542 — `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));` — If neither loaded credentials nor the database yields the referenced credential, this calls `updateEvent` with `undefined`, violating its required dependency and crashing when it reads the credential.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")` — A Google Meet booking with no destination calendar dereferences `undefined` instead of taking the documented fallback path, so this obvious empty-calendar case cannot be booked.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` — If the collective organizer has no destination calendar but another host does, the optional push is a no-op and every available team destination is silently omitted.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 — `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` — Multi-host support remains incomplete for Lark, Office365, and CalDAV because each secondary credential still writes using the first host's calendar ID rather than its own destination.

[booking.destinationCalendar] : user.destinationCalendar ? P1 confidence 100 — packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts:229 — `destinationCalendar: selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []` — The paid-booking creation path likewise retains only one destination, leaving collective teammates without calendar events after payment succeeds.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:454 — `const bookingRef = updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"));` — Cancelling all occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference from each occurrence, leaving the other hosts' recurring events active.

P2 confidence 75 — packages/core/EventManager.ts:554 — `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));` — The booking-merge path deletes only one old calendar event, so merged collective bookings leave stale events in the remaining hosts' calendars.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}),` — The calendar-focused change silently flips unrelated organization-slug persistence based on billing mode, expanding the task into organization provisioning behavior with no traceability to its intent.

P2 confidence 75 — packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:724 — `const loadUsers = async () => {` — Supporting multiple destination calendars does not require replacing the established user-loading flow, removing its organization selection, and remapping its errors, so this unrelated rewrite broadens the booking-path blast radius.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")` — Google Meet bookings with no destination calendar dereference `undefined` in the exact fallback path this branch is meant to handle.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1868 — `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` — Only the first collective host destination is persisted, so confirmation and payment flows that reconstruct the event from the booking permanently lose every additional host calendar.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:171 — `destinationCalendar?: DestinationCalendar[] | null;` — Reusing the webhook-facing `CalendarEvent` field for the new internal collection silently changes the public payload from object/null to array without versioning, breaking existing consumers.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/core/EventManager.ts:376 — `const destinationCalendarCredentials = this.calendarCredentials.filter((c) => c.type === destination.integration)` — Legacy destination rows without `credentialId` now fan out to every account of that type while adapters cannot identify that destination, creating duplicate events in account primary calendars.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156 — `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` — CalDAV creation filters on only the first destination for every credential, so non-primary collective hosts cannot receive events in their selected calendars.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/core/EventManager.ts:554 — `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));` — The merge/reschedule cleanup still deletes only one old calendar reference, leaving all other collective-host events orphaned.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:454 — `const bookingRef = updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"));` — Recurring cancellation repeatedly deletes only each occurrence's first calendar reference inside the new outer reference loop, leaving other host events behind while issuing duplicate delete calls.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254 — `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — When an older reference lacks `externalCalendarId`, the fallback searches for an undefined ID instead of using the event destination, so updates that previously worked now fail.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315 — `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — Legacy deletions fall through to `primary`, and the existing 404 suppression then reports success while leaving an event on its selected secondary calendar.

P2 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:168 — `calendarId: selectedCalendar,` — Creation inserts into `primary` when no selected ID exists but the follow-up Meet patch uses `undefined`, so description enrichment can fail after the event has already been reported successful.

P2 confidence 100 — packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — `const credentialFromDB = await prisma.credential.findUnique({` — Credential lookup is awaited inside the destination loop, producing an avoidable sequential N+1 query path whose latency grows linearly with collective team size.

P2 confidence 100 — packages/core/EventManager.ts:542 — `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));` — A missing referenced credential is passed through as undefined, and the single outer try/catch lets that one stale reference reject the aggregate and misreport every otherwise valid calendar update as failed.

P1 confidence 75 — packages/core/EventManager.ts:353 — `id: destination.credentialId,` — An unscoped destination-calendar credential lookup loads the full OAuth key without verifying user or team ownership, allowing a cross-linked credential ID to make booking creation mutate another tenant's calendar.

P1 confidence 75 — packages/core/EventManager.ts:526 — `id: reference.credentialId,` — Calendar updates resolve booking-reference credential IDs globally rather than against authorized users or teams, so a forged or corrupted reference can use another tenant's OAuth credential to alter external events.

P1 confidence 75 — packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:435 — `id: credentialId,` — The cancellation path globally resolves calendar credentials missing from the organizer's credential set, enabling a cross-tenant booking reference to act as a confused deputy and delete events with another user's OAuth token.

P3 confidence 50 — packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:759 — `throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: error.message });` — The public booking path exposes raw Prisma error messages to clients, potentially disclosing database schema and operational details that the prior centralized error handling could sanitize.

P1 confidence 100 — apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249 — `destinationCalendar: []` — The only changed test merely mirrors the null-to-array serialization change with an empty value, so it passes without exercising collective bookings or proving that multiple host destination calendars are populated and used.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/core/EventManager.ts:339 — `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` — No changed test supplies multiple destinations and verifies one created event/reference per destination, leaving the central multi-calendar creation behavior untested.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/core/EventManager.ts:504 — `for (const reference of calendarReference)` — No changed test covers multi-reference updates, credential lookup fallback, or verifies every referenced calendar is updated, so partial-update regressions can pass.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:423 — `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` — No changed test cancels a booking with multiple calendar references and asserts every remote event is deleted, so orphaned calendar events would go undetected.

P1 confidence 100 — packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147 — `const selectedCalendar = calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId;` — No changed test verifies credential-to-calendar routing or the missing-match `primary` fallback, so events can be silently inserted into the wrong Google calendar while the webhook test remains green.

P2 confidence 75 — packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:727 — `if (!Array.isArray(dynamicUserList) || dynamicUserList.length === 0)` — The new dynamic-user rejection and error-remapping branches have no changed test exercising their status codes or messages, allowing a booking-input compatibility regression to pass.
